dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Post-hypoxic (post-anoxic) myoclonus of subcortical reticular-reflex type, due to global cerebral hypoxic-ischaemic injury following cardiorespiratory arrest.

Alternatives to consider:
1. Lance–Adams syndrome (cortical post-hypoxic myoclonus) — less likely given absent cortical correlate on EEG-EMG back-averaging and normal SSEPs.
2. Myoclonic status epilepticus in the setting of hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy — unlikely as there are no periodic epileptiform discharges and the jerks are chronic rather than acute.
3. Hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy with incidental (non-specific) myoclonus — a non-specific but defensible alternative if the jerks are not felt to constitute a discrete myoclonus syndrome.
